title: Xanadu and HyperLight Cut Optical Switch Loss to 7 mdB Using Thin-Film Lithium Niobate - Quantum Computing Report
gist: Xanadu and HyperLight demonstrated 7 mdB optical switch insertion loss on commercial-wafer thin-film lithium niobate, roughly 3x better than their 2025 result and far below PsiQuantum's published ~100 mdB BTO switches, attacking photonic quantum computing's core loss bottleneck.

insights.claim: Xanadu (NASDAQ/TSX: XNDU) and HyperLight demonstrated a 7 mdB optical switch insertion loss on thin-film lithium niobate (TFLN), nearly a threefold improvement over their 20 mdB milestone in 2025.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: A key component metric for photonic fault tolerance moving fast — positive for XNDU's roadmap credibility.

insights.claim: The 7 mdB result was fabricated on HyperLight's commercial TFLN Chiplet wafer line and verified across high-volume production wafers, indicating repeatability across die yields.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Production-wafer repeatability matters more than hero-device results for scaling.

insights.claim: Xanadu's 7 mdB TFLN switch (fewer than 2 photons lost per 1,000) compares to the ~100 mdB insertion loss PsiQuantum reported in Nature for barium titanate phase shifters on 300 mm silicon wafers (roughly 23 photons lost per 1,000).
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Material-platform choice (TFLN vs BTO) is a key differentiator in the photonic quantum race between Xanadu and PsiQuantum.

insights.claim: Because quantum signals cannot be amplified without destroying coherence, cumulative switch insertion loss rapidly degrades photonic state fidelity, and higher loss demands exponential increases in pump laser power and hardware redundancy to reach error-correction thresholds.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Loss is the gating metric for photonic quantum; small mdB gains have outsized system-level effects.
insights.quote: Higher optical losses require exponential increases in pump laser power and hardware redundancy to compensate for lost qubits before error-correction thresholds can be met.
insights.locator: In photonic quantum architectures, optical switches

insights.claim: While barium titanate has high electro-optic Pockels coefficients, thin-film lithium niobate benefits from mature commercial manufacturing already deployed in high-bandwidth optical interconnects for AI and telecom networks.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Riding the AI/telecom TFLN supply chain may give Xanadu a manufacturing-scale advantage.

insights.claim: Minimizing switch loss underpins Xanadu's strategy of running room-temperature photonic computing networks without massive cryo-refrigeration overhead.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Room-temperature operation is a potential cost advantage versus cryogenic modalities.
insights.locator: Minimizing switch insertion loss is central

insights.claim: Xanadu and HyperLight said the ultra-low-loss TFLN switching platform could offer power-efficiency advantages for optical routing in energy-intensive enterprise AI data centers.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Optionality for a non-quantum revenue line in AI optical interconnects.
insights.locator: Minimizing switch insertion loss is central
